overall: The Commission violated the Open Meeting Law by posting an insufficiently specific notice (no street address, wrong year) but did not violate it by discussing an unlisted sidewalk topic the chair did not anticipate.

allegations.summary: The Dec. 2, 2015 meeting notice allegedly lacked the street address of the meeting location and listed the year as 2016 instead of 2015.
allegations.key_passage: For this reason, the notice did not comply with the Open Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: A sidewalk project was discussed at the meeting under 'Other new business' though it was not listed on the notice.
allegations.key_passage: Because the Chair did not anticipate that the sidewalk project would be discussed at the meeting, the Commission did not violate the Open Meeting Law in this respect.

allegations.summary: Commission members allegedly acted in a hostile manner toward members of the public during the meeting.
allegations.key_passage: This allegation, even if true, would not constitute a violation of G.L. c. 30A, §§ 18-25.

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law.
remedy_passage: We order the Commission's immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law, and we caution that similar future violations may be considered evidence of intent to violate the law.
note: Read by a language model from the letter; every key passage is checked verbatim against it and dropped if not. A holding is the Attorney General’s reading of the law in this case only.
